b: Enoch is shown the fall of the Watchers, the Nephilim, heaven and hell, and the coming judgment. Quoted in Jude 14–15 and found among the Dead Sea Scrolls. Canon in the Ethiopian church.
Enoch tours ten heavens and returns to teach his sons. Survives only in Old Slavonic.
cr: W. R. Morfill & R. H. Charles (1896), public domain

b: Genesis and early Exodus retold by an angel to Moses, dated in 49-year "jubilees." Many copies were found at Qumran. Canon in the Ethiopian church.
A Hebrew retelling of Genesis through Joshua. It borrows the name of the lost book cited in Joshua 10:13, but scholars date this text to the Middle Ages.
Baruch wrestles with why Jerusalem fell and is shown the age to come. Written after the temple was destroyed in AD 70.
Baruch is led through five heavens by an angel.
Moses' farewell prophecy to Joshua. Jude 9 may allude to its lost ending.
Isaiah's martyrdom (sawn in two, cf. Hebrews 11:37) and his vision of the seven heavens.
Eighteen psalms from the time Rome took Jerusalem. Psalm 17 is a key pre-Christian picture of the Messiah.
Extra psalms preserved in Syriac. Hebrew originals of some turned up in the Dead Sea Psalms Scroll.
cr: 19th-century translation from the Syriac, public domain

b: Abraham rejects his father's idols and ascends to see the throne of God and the future.
Abraham refuses to die and is given a tour of the world and the judgment of souls.
Job retells his story to his children, with Satan as his direct opponent.
Solomon uses a ring from the archangel Michael to command demons to build the temple.
How Joseph's Egyptian wife Aseneth (Genesis 41:45) turned from idols.
A wise Assyrian vizier betrayed by his nephew. Ahikar appears in Tobit; an Aramaic copy was found at Elephantine in Egypt.

t: History of the Rechabites (Narrative of Zosimus)
b: A hermit visits the blessed descendants of the Rechabites of Jeremiah 35.
Sedrach argues with God about mercy for sinners.

d: c. 2nd century BC, with later Christian additions
b: The deathbed words of Reuben, son of Jacob, to his children. Part of the Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs.

b: The deathbed words of Benjamin, son of Jacob, to his children. Part of the Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs.
The birth and childhood of Mary and the birth of Jesus. Source of the names Joachim and Anna.
Miracle stories of Jesus as a child aged five to twelve. Not the same book as the Coptic Gospel of Thomas.
A Latin infancy gospel; source of the ox and donkey at the manger.
Jesus tells the disciples about the life and death of Joseph.
Infancy miracles, including Jesus speaking in the cradle (a story also in the Quran).

t: Acts of Pilate (Gospel of Nicodemus, part 1)
b: An expanded account of the trial of Jesus before Pilate.
The "harrowing of hell": Christ frees Adam and the patriarchs from Hades.
A letter put in Pilate's mouth reporting Jesus to the emperor.
Pilate's supposed report on the crucifixion and its wonders.
A legend of how Pilate died.
A legend tying the fall of Jerusalem to the crucifixion.
Joseph of Arimathea's story of the two thieves and the burial.
Thecla hears Paul, leaves her fiancé and survives the arena. Contains the famous physical description of Paul.
Thomas is sold as a slave and carries the gospel to India.
Andrew rescues Matthias from a city of cannibals.
Peter and Paul in Rome, their contest with Simon Magus, and their deaths.
The travels and martyrdom of Philip.
John Mark tells of Barnabas's mission and death on Cyprus.
King Abgar of Edessa, his letter to Jesus, and the image on the cloth.
The earliest Christian tour of heaven and hell. It was nearly included in the New Testament; the Muratorian list mentions it.
What Paul saw when "caught up to the third heaven" (2 Corinthians 12). It shaped medieval ideas of hell, including Dante's.

t: Apocalypse of Moses (Life of Adam and Eve)
b: Adam and Eve after Eden: Eve's own account of the fall, Adam's death and burial.
Ezra pleads with God for sinners and sees the punishments.
A second, later apocalypse written in John's name.
The death and assumption of the Virgin Mary.
A letter from the church in Rome to Corinth. One of the oldest Christian writings outside the New Testament; it was bound into Codex Alexandrinus.
The oldest surviving Christian sermon outside the New Testament.
A first-century church manual: the Two Ways, baptism, fasting, the Lord's Prayer and the Eucharist. Rediscovered in 1873.
Reads the Old Testament as allegory pointing to Christ. Bound into Codex Sinaiticus right after Revelation.
A freed slave in Rome receives visions about repentance. Hugely popular; bound into Codex Sinaiticus.
Twelve commandments given by the Shepherd.
Ten parables, including the tower that is the church.
Written on the road to martyrdom in Rome. This edition prints the shorter (genuine) and longer (expanded) versions together.
On unity under the bishop. Shorter and longer versions together.
Against those who said Christ only seemed to suffer. Shorter and longer versions together.
He begs the Roman church not to save him from the beasts. Shorter and longer versions together.
Shorter and longer versions together.
First known use of the phrase "catholic church." Shorter and longer versions together.
Advice from one bishop to another. Shorter and longer versions together.
By a man said to have known the apostle John. Quotes much of the New Testament.
The oldest account of a Christian martyrdom outside the New Testament.
An elegant defense of Christianity to a pagan inquirer.
The earliest statements about who wrote Mark and Matthew.
114 sayings of Jesus with no story around them. About half have parallels in Matthew, Mark and Luke. Nag Hammadi Codex II.
A Valentinian collection on sacraments and the "bridal chamber." Nag Hammadi Codex II.
A meditation on Jesus as the one who ends ignorance of the Father. Often linked to Valentinus. Nag Hammadi Codex I.
Mary Magdalene comforts the disciples and shares a vision; Peter doubts her. From the Berlin Codex (found 1896), not Nag Hammadi. Pages 1–6 and 11–14 are lost.
Jesus' private talks with Judas, in a Sethian Gnostic frame. From Codex Tchacos, not Nag Hammadi.
